issues.description: The problem statement contains an internal contradiction about which SealSaloon methods should be static. The UML fragment (problem_statement.md) lists calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) as ordinary public methods (no static marker), while the textual requirements later (lines 77–80) explicitly require calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery to be static. This inconsistency in the specification (instance vs. static methods) can confuse students about the correct signatures and where to place these methods (instance vs. class-level) and may lead to implementations that don't match the provided reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the UML in problem_statement.md to mark calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery as static (or indicate in the diagram/text that they are class-level methods), or (B) remove the textual requirement that they must be static and keep them as instance methods. Ensure the example/reference solution and any tests use the same choice so students have a single unambiguous target.
